question.:question/problem: Calculate the flux of the vector field $F(x,y)={y}^{3}\,i+(2+x)\,j$ across the closed curve $C$ given by $r(t)=4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field and $C$ is a piecewise-smooth, simple, closed curve, then the flux of $F$ across $C$ is given by

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x,
$$

where $n$ denotes the outward-pointing unit normal vector to $C.$ 

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=4\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x,y) & ={y}^{3}=8{sin}^{3}⁡t, \\ Q(x,y) & =2+x=2+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ along the curve, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡t)=-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t, \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral using the substitution $\operatorname{sin}⁡t=u,du=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,dt,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(P\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}-Q\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }(8{sin}^{3}⁡t)\cdot (2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)-(2+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\cdot (-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }16{sin}^{3}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+8\operatorname{sin}⁡t+16\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }8\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }16{sin}^{3}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+16\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }8\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{0}16{u}^{3}+16u\,\text{d}u \\  & =-8\operatorname{cos}⁡t{|}_{0}^{2\pi }+0 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∬}_{D}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}A,
$$

which is equivalent to

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A.

question.:question/problem:
Use the flux form of Green's theorem to calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
F(x,y)=\left\langle 28 x y, \; 12 x^{2} y + 2 \sin{\left(x \right)} \right\rangle

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $F=P\,i+Q\,j,$ and $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then the flux form of Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∬}_{D}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}A,
$$

which is equivalent to

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

$$

$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$

$$

question.:question/problem:
A curve is defined by the parametric equations

$$
x=2 t+5,\qquad y=t^{3}+5 t,\qquad -\infty<t<\infty.
$$

Calculate the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point where $t=-2.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find the coordinates of the point by substituting $t=-2$ into the parametric equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2 (-2)+5=-4+5=1 \\ y & =(-2)^{3}+5 (-2)=-8-10=-18\end{aligned}
$$

So we're looking to find the equation of the tangent line to the curve at the point $(1,-18).$

To find the slope of the tangent line, we need to find $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}.$ To compute it, we first need to find the derivatives of $x$ and $y,$ as follows:

$$
x'(t)=2,\qquad y'(t)=3 t^{2}+5.
$$

So, we have

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}=\frac{3 t^{2}+5}{2}.
$$

At the point where $t=-2,$ the slope of the tangent line is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{3 (-2)^{2}+5}{2}=\frac{17}{2}=\frac{17}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to calculate the equation of the tangent line, we use point-slope form with the point $(x_1,y_1)=(1,-18)$ and the slope $m=\frac{17}{2}.$ We get

$$
y+18=\frac{17}{2}(x-1).
$$
